This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 03.12.2023 at about 1.15 p.m. he had been going to take a bath in Nethravathi River, near SCCH-5 Nethravathi Snanaghatta, Dharmasthala Village,
Belthangady Taluk, Dakshina Kannada.

At that time, a driver of the car bearing Reg.
No.KL-60-C-9418 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Benaka Health Centre, thereafter shifted to Ujire Multi Speciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards medical expenses.

3. At the time of the accident, he was aged about 19 years, hale and healthy, working as office boy at Maithri Information System, Bengaluru thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. due to this accident he cannot continue his work and lost his future income.

Out of this accident crime No.114/2023 is registered against the driver of the SCCH-5 said offending car before the Belthangadi Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the said offending car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-
with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

Further admitted issuance of insurance policy vide No.76180031230100010989 valid from 29.10.2023 to 28.10.2024 in respect of Maruti Alto bearing Reg. No.KL-60-C-9418, which is valid as on the date of accident.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.
Further denied that alleged SCCH-5 accident was occurred due to negligency on the part of the offending car.

Further submitted that, driver of the insured had no valid driving licence as on the date of accident.,
thereby committed breach of policy conditions.

There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6)
of M.V.Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.2 remained absent, hence placed exparte.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:

sentences.text: 1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 03.12.2023 at abut 1.15 p.m. near Nethravathi Snanaghatta, Dharmasthala Village, Belthangady, Dakshina Kannada due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.

No.KL-0-C-9418 dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH-5 2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1 and marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- SCCH-5 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.5,
copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.9.
9.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, sketch,
mahazar, Sec.133 notice, reply, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 03.12.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5 10.

Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondent No.1 has not taken any endeavors to Dinesh K T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30910284/

sentences.text: 3 disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 03.12.2023 at about 1.15 p.m. when he was walking near Nethravathi Snanaghatta, Dharmasthala Village,
Belthangadi Taluk, Dakshina Kannada.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KL-60-C-9418.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence SCCH-5 of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 19 years, to prove his age,
petitioner has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.10, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 14.04.2004, the alleged accident was occurred on 03.12.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.10, age of the petitioner is considered as 20 years as on the date of the accident.

Further petitioner was working as Office Boy at Maithri Information System, thereby earning Rs.20,000/-
p.m.
In this regard, petitioner has not produced any income proof documents.
SCCH-5 13.
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained right wrist distal radius fracture

To prove the same, petitioner has exhibited copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Benaka health Centre, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.11, medical bills to the tune of Rs.7,386/-
marked as Ex.P.12, ECG Films marked as Ex.P.13 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.14.
14.
Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated him nor produced the disability certificate towards the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

but on perusal of the facts,
wound certificate and evidence of PW-1 corroborated to believe the injuries sustained by the petitioner out of the accident.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.50,000/- along with medical bills of Rs.7,386/- and Rs.20,000/- on head of pain and suffering.
Further on SCCH-5 perusal of medical records i.e., wound certificate etc., confers to the court about causing of pain and suffering to the petitioner out of the accident as alleged in the petition.
15. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.77,386/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

16. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.76180031230100010989 which is valid for the period from 29.10.2023 to 28.10.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 03.12.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.2 shall go against respondent No.1, so that, respondent No.1/insurer is directed to SCCH-5 deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.

With these views, I have answered Issue Dinesh K T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30910284/
4 No.2 partly in the affirmative.

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.77,386/-
(Rupees Seventy Seven Thousand Three Hundred Eighty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to his SCCH-5 account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
